# What a coding agent is

A coding agent works directly on the files in a folder, whereas a chat window works only on what is pasted or uploaded into the conversation. It is therefore more useful for preparing teaching material, and because it can change and delete files it needs closer supervision.

|  | Chat window | Coding agent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What it sees | What you paste or upload | Every file in the folder you open it in |
| What it produces | Text in the conversation | Files on disk: notes, slides, notebooks, spreadsheets |
| Running code | Limited or none | Runs what is installed on your machine (Python, R, Stata, LaTeX) and reads the result |
| Continuity | Depends on what you re-supply or what the product remembers | Reads a standing instruction file at the start of every session |
| Scale | One document at a time | A whole module, or a folder of scripts, in one task |

**Products.** Anthropic, OpenAI and Google each offer a coding agent alongside their chat products: Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI. The chapters that follow apply to all three. The notes headed *In Claude Code* give the specifics for one of them, and the other two have equivalent settings under different names.

**In practice.** You can ask for a problem set and its solutions, have the solutions executed, and get back the files with the numerical answers already checked. You can ask for the notation in ten weeks of slides to be made consistent. Neither is practical by copying and pasting.

**Limits.** The model still makes confident mistakes: a sign error in a derivation, a reference that does not exist, a question that is harder than intended. Running code catches numerical errors but not a wrong economic argument. Chapter 8 covers checking.

**Permissions.** Because the agent can edit and delete files, every product has a setting for what it may do without asking. For a first module:

- Open the agent in a folder made for the module and never in your home folder.
- Begin in the mode that asks before each edit, and relax it once you have seen how the agent behaves.
- Keep the folder under version control or in a synced drive with file history, so any change can be undone.

> **In Claude Code.** It runs in a terminal, a desktop app, VS Code, JetBrains IDEs and the browser ([platforms](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/platforms)). The desktop app is the easiest start for colleagues who do not use a terminal.
>
> The [permission modes](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes) are Manual (asks before edits and commands), `acceptEdits` (edits files in the folder without asking), `plan` (reads and proposes, changes nothing until you approve) and `auto` (acts without asking, with a separate model reviewing its actions). Recent versions start interactive terminal and VS Code sessions in `auto`, so switch to Manual or `plan` for a first session. In the terminal, Shift+Tab cycles through the modes.
